status.en: 244 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Lagos, Abuja and Plateau State.
status.nb: 244 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Lagos, Abuja og Plateau State.

summary.en: Gunmen continue to raid villages in northeast and eastern Nigeria, killing at least ten civilians and looting shops, while a separate attack on a village after Friday prayers left twenty dead and later rose to forty. Bandits attacked women harvesting groundnuts in Plateau, killing a woman and injuring two farmers. Community hunters in Katsina killed fourteen bandits and foiled a kidnap plot, and hunters in another area killed fourteen suspected bandits. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenmenn fortsetter å raidere landsbyer i nordøst- og Øst-Nigeria, og dreper minst ti sivile og plyndrer butikker, mens et separat angrep på en landsby etter fredagsbønnene etterlot tjue døde og senere økte tallet til førti. Banditter angrep kvinner som høstet jordnøtter i Plateau, drepte en kvinne og såret to bønder. Lokale jegere i Katsina drepte fjorten banditter og avverget et kidnappingforsøk, og jegere i et annet område drepte fjorten mistenkte banditter. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
